scientific_summary: In stable treated adult inflammatory myopathy, the reported six-month ITT-LOCF timed-function comparison favored the tested creatine monohydrate added to shared home exercise. A separate older-adult training study found lean-mass benefit without an added strength advantage; neither erases the earlier DMD/FSHD evidence.

exact_prior_decision.route: Creatine monohydrate / pediatric muscle-strength compensation comparator
exact_prior_decision.disposition: Prioritize a substantive pediatric strength/energetics compensation comparison; mixed functional outcomes and MVA efficacy unresolved
exact_prior_decision.evidence_scope: Earlier DMD: complete original abstracts of PMID 15159476, 15984021 and 20395096, plus current CINRG registry protocol only; scientific mains/native outcomes remain unqualified. Separately, 2025 FSHD PMID 40366059: complete scientific XML main/tables, all native main figures, full supplied SAP text, all native supplementary PDF pages and complete current registry, independently reviewed. Native publisher main PDF/table pixels and historical registry fields remain unverified; no fresh DMD or corpus-wide reading credit.
exact_prior_decision.rationale: Three original randomized DMD abstracts provide selected pediatric strength evidence: the 2004 crossover reports dominant-hand grip and fat-free-mass increases during treatment, with the exact placebo-adjusted/period contrast unresolved; functional tasks and activities of daily living did not improve. The 2010 trial reports between-group manual-strength change (P=.04) and an adjusted PCr/Pi difference (P=.03), with a functional-scale null (P=.19) and vitamin C as comparator. The larger six-month CINRG trial reports nonsignificant primary manual/quantitative strength comparisons; its individual secondary results remain unread. Full scientific mains were inaccessible, limiting effect-size, carryover, multiplicity and safety adjudication. Current registry NCT00016653 confirms monohydrate and separate oral arms but differs in enrollment/date fields and posts no results. These actual pediatric strength signals challenge niacin on direct functional evidence; the restoration rationale and apitegromab’s stronger documented SMA motor comparison are different dimensions, not proof of MVA superiority. Prioritize fair relevant-model comparison without claiming BUBR1 restoration, genotype rescue or equivalence across creatine preparations. The independently qualified 2025 pediatric FSHD crossover adds 13 randomized children and 11 two-period completers, without assuming complete pairs or equal secondary denominators. Its primary MFM-32 creatine–placebo estimate was +0.19 points (95% CI −0.71 to 1.08; supplementary P=.68), with no demonstrated motor-function benefit. Secondary walking was +27.74 m (−1.41 to 56.88; P=.06); favorable FSHD-COM and timed-walk estimates were also uncertain, and PUL/MRI intervals crossed zero. This primary null does not erase the earlier DMD positives or prove generic ineffectiveness. Serum creatinine rose and creatinine-derived eGFR fell; the authors’ production explanation and reported reversal establish neither renal injury nor unaffected filtration without independent confirmation. Small enrollment, late supplied SAP, missingness, unadjusted multiplicity, current-registry/reporting inconsistencies and unsettled carryover remain explicit. These findings refine the mixed-evidence compensation comparison without a nominee change, MVA efficacy or BUBR1-restoration claim.
exact_prior_decision.identity_limit: Exact monohydrate alias has no current main-catalog join. Generic creatine maps separately to CHEMBL283800 as a moiety reference, not an efficacy alias. NIH DSLD397 contains the monohydrate synonym; broader group membership is not preparation equivalence, availability, approval or efficacy.

source_qualification.source_specific_disposition: Add adult stable inflammatory-myopathy functional benefit and distinct older-adult lean-mass benefit with strength nulls; preserve prior pediatric DMD and FSHD evidence separately. No nominee change or MVA transfer.

sources.title: Creatine supplements in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies who are clinically weak after conventional pharmacologic treatment: Six-month, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
sources.depth: Complete authentic nine-page scientific main PDF, all native pages/tables/figures/captions/funding read.
sources.source_identity: Title, authors, DOI, journal, year, pages and abstract matched original PMID metadata; public Myositis Association host, not publisher download.

sources.title: Impact of creatine supplementation in combination with resistance training on lean mass in the elderly
sources.publication: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle 2016;7:413–421
sources.depth: Complete original scientific XML and authentic nine-page open-access article PDF; all native pages/main tables/figures/captions/disclosures read.
sources.source_identity: Public PDF mirror matched original XML title/authors/DOI/pages, study flow and native tables. Mirror host does not establish trial-product equivalence.

design.population: Men and women over 18 with polymyositis/dermatomyositis for more than six months, stable low disease activity but persistent clinical weakness after conventional treatment; quadriceps at least 20% below expected by clinician assessment; enough mobility for exercise. Inclusion-body myositis and serious renal/liver disease excluded.
design.recruitment: 1999–2003, two randomized centers: London and Stockholm/Malmo clinical services.
design.randomization: Hospital-pharmacy random-number lists, centers randomized separately, no stratification; identical containers, allocation concealed until trial ended and statistical analysis completed; patients/clinicians/assessors blinded.
design.completer_arm_counts: Not specified in the native flowchart; Table 2 headers 19/18 are randomized groups and must not be assigned to VCC denominators.
design.drug_context: Prior systemic steroids at least 6 months; current prednisolone stable 2 months and immunosuppressants stable 3 months if used. Azathioprine/methotrexate reported. No inference to untreated or active severe disease.

exposure.preparation: Highly purified creatine monohydrate obtained from Flamma Ltd, Bergamo, Italy
exposure.placebo: Same manufacturer, lactose plus other inert constituents; full excipient composition and calorie matching not specified.
exposure.cointervention: Both groups: home resistance work for upper/lower limbs, neck/trunk plus range of motion, stretching and 15-minute walk; prescribed 5 days/week. Compliance assessed by patient interviews each visit, without objective achieved-volume records.
exposure.identity_limit: Supplier/preparation stated; exact batch/purity percentage not reported. No generic nutrient, retail or cross-study batch equivalence.
exposure.placebo_dosing: Matching 20 g/day for eight days, then 3 g/day oral schedule in Methods; equal mass is not established calorie equivalence.

primary.endpoint: Aggregate functional performance time (AFPT), sum in seconds of 50-foot walk, get-up-and-go including 50-foot walk, 19-step ascent and 19-step descent; lower is better.
primary.analysis: ITT with last observation carried forward; between-group Mann–Whitney U test of percentage change from baseline. Within-arm Wilcoxon tests kept separate.

body_ITT_percent_changes.locator: Native page 697, Results: Comparisons between groups at 6 months

primary.reporting_limit: Abstract labels rounded values resembling completer estimates as ITT; Results gives different ITT medians/ranges. Figure 2A caption calls graph ITT. Preserve all source attributions; no participant-level resolution or estimate reconstructed from graph pixels.
primary.treatment_effect_CI: Not provided for the primary between-arm comparison.
primary.three_months: Median changes −10.9% active versus −5.1% placebo; between-arm difference not significant, despite within-arm improvements.
primary.interpretation: Credited randomized functional positive at 6 months in this treated adult population; not disease cure, restoration, or proof of benefit without exercise. AFPT not fully validated in IIM and emphasizes lower-limb tasks.

functional_index.within_P_prose_discrepancy: Prose uses active P = .034 in ITT narrative, whereas native Table 2 assigns .034 to VCC and .012 to ITT.
functional_index.percent_change_contrasts: No between-group difference for percent changes in either ITT or completer analysis.
functional_index.limitation: Endpoint-score completer signal and within-arm improvements do not replace the ITT between-arm null; ceiling at 64 noted.

MMT.role: Secondary bilateral ordinal muscle scores; native Table 3 six-month results labeled ITT; no reported multiple-testing adjustment or adjusted change-score treatment estimate.
MMT.interpretation: Retain actual secondary shoulder/hip strength positives without promoting all muscle groups or treating nominal repeated comparisons as independent trials.
MMT.source_precision: Native Table 3 includes an elbow upper quartile 5.50 despite the described 0–5 scale; not corrected.

other_nulls: CK and inflammatory/laboratory measures as reported

biomarkers.abstract_threshold: P < .05 versus main/figure P = .05 at 6 months
biomarkers.interpretation: One arm reaching a P threshold while another does not is not a between-treatment effect or proof that metabolite change mediates functional benefit.

missingness_and_hierarchy.sample_size: Initial reasoning used five-person uncontrolled pilot/within-group strength variability; planned 56 including 20% attrition, enrolled 37 because recruitment could not extend beyond 4 years. Reported 75% power was post hoc.
missingness_and_hierarchy.pilot: Five patients, 20 g/day for 2 weeks, uncontrolled AFPT/PCr changes; hypothesis-generating context only, not a second efficacy appraisal.
missingness_and_hierarchy.multiplicity: Multiple muscle groups, timepoints, patient-reported measures and biomarkers; no correction described.
missingness_and_hierarchy.registration: No identifier in authentic main. Exact ClinicalTrials.gov PMID/DOI query returned zero; no authenticated trial registry, original protocol or SAP obtained. This is not proof of no registration anywhere.

harms.arm_split: Six to seven per group stated; exact active/placebo split not supplied.
harms.attribution: Authors considered none related to creatine or other IIM medication; no unrestricted safety inference.
harms.laboratories: Authors report no significant ESR, CK or creatinine change within/between groups at 3/6 months. Renal/liver disease excluded and small sample limits detection.

disclosure.supplier: Flamma Ltd; not assumed free supply or funding beyond stated methods.
disclosure.COI: No explicit author conflict-of-interest declaration located in the nine-page main; do not convert absence of a declaration into no conflicts.

design.population: Nonathletic men and women 60–80 years, nonvegetarian, not in systematic exercise; renal/liver/heart disease and medications affecting growth/training excluded. Some participants used antihypertensive, diabetes, thyroid and hormone therapies.
design.analysis_limit: Completer analysis of 27; no ITT imputation reported. Methods overview uses 13/14 as assigned counts, but Results/native flow clearly show 16/16 randomized.
design.allocation: Random assignment 1:1 stated; exact sequence-generation method not described. Coded packages supplied by staff outside data acquisition/analysis.
design.power: Achieved lean-mass effect size .99/power 80% calculated retrospectively; not a prospective adequate-power guarantee for strength.

exposure.preparation: Creatine monohydrate powder from MEDNUTRITION INC., Brazil; tested sample 99.7% pure by HPLC
exposure.training_days: Main describes supplement packages dissolved in a beverage containing 100 g lemon-flavoured maltodextrin after resistance training, for both groups. Current registry explicitly describes active 5 g creatine + 100 g maltodextrin versus placebo 100 g maltodextrin total.
exposure.control_quantity_limit: Whether placebo packet adds another 5 g on training days is ambiguous between main and registry; do not silently resolve 105 g versus 100 g or assert calorie equivalence. On nontraining days active 5 g creatine versus 5 g maltodextrin.
exposure.cointervention: Both groups supervised resistance exercise 3 days/week, about 60 min/session, 12 weeks after familiarization; progressive upper/lower-limb/core exercises, similar protocol.
exposure.diet: Habitual diet; 3-day records showed no significant between-arm energy/macronutrient/calcium change. Not proof of exact supplement calorie matching.
exposure.identity_limit: Measured sample purity does not prove cross-trial batch/retail equivalence; no creatine-only/no-exercise arm or formal synergy estimate.

primary.hierarchy: Lean mass by DXA and strength by 10 RM bench/leg press are co-primary as described in main; no multiplicity adjustment described.
primary.analysis: Delta (post–pre) scores compared by Student t-test or Mann–Whitney according to distribution; α = .05; no treatment CI reported.
primary.within_strength: Both groups improved; native Table 3 P = .001 versus prose P < .0001. Neither within-arm change supplies creatine-specific strength benefit.
primary.interpretation: Lean-mass positive retained as body-composition evidence; primary strength comparisons null at this sample/exposure. DXA nonfat/nonbone tissue does not demonstrate muscle-fibre renewal or separate hydration from contractile tissue.

secondary.category_limit: Descriptive only; not a prespecified confirmed clinical cure or independent functional effect. Gait/handgrip thresholds used diagnostically without reported separate randomized continuous-outcome contrasts.

harms.collection: Self-report checked 3 times/week with researcher contact access
harms.findings: No self-reported creatine-induced side effects. Both groups reported exercise-related muscle pain, limb swelling and reduced range of motion. Counts/severity by arm not supplied.
harms.renal_limit: Renal/liver/heart disease excluded; no renal-function laboratory outcome described. Does not establish universal or MVA safety.

registry.reading: Official current-page web-reader representation; direct raw request 403; no fresh live-field or historical-version certification.
registry.timing_limit: Registration after reported intervention period; outcomes include results in current representation. Does not verify prospective analytic choices.
registry.eligibility_mismatch: Registry requires sarcopenia; main includes broader healthy/nonathletic cohort with only some sarcopenia-stage classifications.
registry.outcome_descriptions: Registry lists at least 10% mass and 50% strength pre/post increases plus later observed results; between-arm comparison, not within-arm success descriptions, is the causal contrast.
registry.ethics_mismatch: Paper 840.317 versus registry 653443 plus Plataforma Brasil identifier; not reconciled without source history.

pinto2016.disclosure: FAPEG support and MedNutrition supplement supply acknowledged; authors declare no conflicts. No sponsor-role details beyond main reported.

separate_contexts: Adult chronic treated polymyositis/dermatomyositis with home exercise
Previously qualified pediatric FSHD primary trial
comparative_interpretation.function: Chung supplies a reported between-arm objective functional positive with secondary proximal strength signals and stated uncertainty. Pinto supplies lean-mass benefit but not demonstrated added strength. Neither erases the other or earlier DMD/FSHD results.
comparative_interpretation.mechanism: No between-treatment MRS estimate or mediation established; no muscle energetic assay in Pinto. No BUB1B/BUBR1, chromosome-fidelity or renewal outcome.
comparative_interpretation.fair_bar: Use same function/exposure/durability/renewal/fidelity criteria for compensation candidates; BUBR1 mediation additionally required only for restoration claims. No automatic preference for existing nominees.

historical_metadata_notice: The nested source qualification is the exact frozen historical object, including its pending-review label and 037570fc/275 identity checkpoint. Separate independent ACCEPT and current c61fc087/276 proposal context are recorded here; historical scientific fields were not rewritten.

source_provenance.raw_assets: Retained externally in the named source archive; no original primary PDFs, raw XML, registry payloads or native images are copied into this portable export.

reading_attribution.source_and_independent_depth: Producer read both complete scientific mains and all 18 native main PDF pages; independent reviewer read both complete scientific mains and 11 selected native pages. Saved registry representation and plan/access limitations are retained; no fresh DMD/FSHD source reading.
reading_attribution.portable_synthesis: Accepted qualifications, independent reviews, immutable ledger and targeted document passages read. No new primary-source or native-panel reading at this stage.
reading_attribution.earlier_studies: Old source-specific reading depth is preserved; citations and inherited rationale confer no new reading credit.

interpretive_boundaries: Separate preparations, populations, exercise/background treatment and durations; no pooled efficacy or generic retail equivalence.
No MVA efficacy, genotype rescue, healthy-tissue renewal or chromosome-fidelity claim.
Compensation evidence receives the same function, exposure, durability, renewal and fidelity criteria; BUBR1 mediation additionally applies to restoration claims.
